ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which node of the jsoup document the walk into the W3C builder starts from, and only that node is walked; hop 1 only sets the document URI from the location, and hops 2-4 pass the document and the visitor along unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises a walk of the jsoup document into a visitor that builds a W3C DOM document from it, and on namespaces.xhtml (a leading Comment from its <?xml ...?> line, then <html>) the walk covers that comment alone: no element of the document reaches the builder and no W3C document of it is built. Nothing below the gold can recover the elements: a builder that skips the early comment leaves the W3C document empty, and one that appends it to the W3C document leaves only the comment there. Nothing above the gold restores the start: the gold takes a jsoup Document, so a hop cannot hand it the root element (Element is not a Document), the visitor is a W3CBuilder that no hop outside org.jsoup.helper can create, and normalising or cloning the document keeps the leading comment. The convention is pinned outside the gold: W3CDom.convert, the public sibling performing the same two steps, starts at in.child(0) ('skip the #root node'); Evaluator.IsRoot.matches takes child(0) of a Document as its root; Element.child and Element.children ('effectively a filter on childNodes() to get Element nodes') define child(0) as the first element child. Passing tests: W3CDomTest convertsGoogle (the W3C document of a document that begins with a doctype starts at its html element), CssTest root (:root is the html element), ElementTest testChildrenElements and testChildThrowsIndexOutOfBoundsOnMissing.
